en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Ninth Chapter
Is the object of the deathless a fetter? Yes.
Is the Deathless subject to fetters, subject to ties, subject to floods, subject to yokes, subject to hindrances, adhered to, subject to clinging, and subject to defilement?
One should not say so...
[as before] ...Is it not the case that the Deathless is not subject to fetters, not subject to ties... [as before] ...and not subject to defilement?
“Yes.
“If it is so that the Deathless is not a fetter, ... [and so on] ... is not subject to defilement, then surely you should not say:
‘The object of the Deathless is a fetter.’”
Is lust aroused with reference to the Deathless? Yes.
Is the Deathless a basis for lust, a thing that causes lust, that incites passion, that intoxicates, that binds, and that deludes?
It should not be said so...
[as before] ...Is it not the case that the Deathless is not a basis for lust, not provocative of passion, not desirable, not intoxicating, not binding, and not delusive?
Yes, it is.
If the Deathless is not a basis for lust, not provocative of passion, not desirable, not intoxicating, not binding, and not deluding,
then surely it should not be said that "lust arises with reference to the Deathless.
Does hatred arise with reference to the Deathless?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Then is the Deathless a state of hatred, a state of anger, and a state of aversion?
You should not speak thus … [and so on] …
Is it not the case that the Deathless is not a basis for hatred, not a basis for anger, and not a basis for resentment?
Yes, it is.
If indeed the Deathless is not a basis for hatred, not a basis for anger, and not a basis for resentment, then surely you should not say: [that it is otherwise].
“Hatred arises with reference to the Deathless.
Does delusion arise with reference to the Deathless? Yes.
Is the Deathless a basis for delusion, a cause of ignorance, a cause of lack of vision, an obstruction to wisdom, on the side of affliction, and not conducive to Nibbāna?
You should not say so...

[and so forth] ...Is it not rather the case that the Deathless is not a basis for delusion, not a cause of ignorance, not a cause of lack of vision, an increase of wisdom, not on the side of affliction, and conducive to Nibbāna?
“Yes.
“If it is so that the Deathless is not a basis for delusion, does not cause ignorance,
[and so on] … leads to Nibbāna, then indeed, sir, you should not say:”
“Delusion arises with reference to the Deathless.
Do fetters arise with reference to form? Is form a thing that fetters, a thing that binds, ... [and so on] ... a thing that defiles? Yes.
“Fetters arise with reference to the Deathless; is the Deathless a thing that fetters... [and so on] ...is it subject to defilement?
One should not say this... [and so on].
“Does lust arise with reference to form; is form a basis for lust, a thing that causes passion, that is desirable, intoxicating, binding, and delusive?”
“Yes,” you say.
“Does lust arise with reference to the Deathless? Is the Deathless a basis for lust … [and so on] … a basis for infatuation?
You must not say so … [and so on].
Taking form as an object, hatred arises; is form a basis for hatred, a basis for anger, and a basis for aversion? Yes.
Taking the Deathless as an object, hatred arises; is the Deathless a basis for hatred, a basis for anger, and a basis for aversion?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Does delusion arise with reference to form? Is form a basis for delusion, a cause of ignorance … [as before] … leading away from Nibbāna? Yes.
Does delusion arise with reference to the Deathless? Is the Deathless a basis for delusion, a cause of ignorance? ... [as before] ... does it not lead to Nibbāna?
You should not say so. ...
Does fettering arise with reference to the Deathless? Is the Deathless unfettering, unentangling, unobstructing, unyoking, non-obscuring, unclinging-to, non-grasping, and non-defiling?
“Yes,” you say.
“Do fetters arise with reference to form? Is form not subject to fettering, not subject to knotting, and so on, up to: not subject to defilement?
You should not speak thus … [as before] … .
Lust arises with reference to the Deathless; is the Deathless not a basis for lust, not provocative of lust, not desirable, not intoxicating, not binding, and not delusive?
Yes. Lust arises with reference to form; is form not a basis for lust... [and so on]? Yes.
“Is it not the case that one does not become infatuated with the Deathless? “One should not say so…” [and so on].
“Does hatred arise with reference to the Deathless? Is the Deathless not a basis for hatred, not a basis for anger, and not a basis for aversion?”
“Yes,” you say.
“But does hatred arise with reference to form, while form itself is not a basis for hatred, not a basis for anger, and not a basis for resentment?
You must not say so… [and so on].
Delusion arises with reference to the Deathless; is the Deathless not a basis for delusion, not a cause of ignorance, and so forth... does it lead to Nibbāna? Yes.
Does delusion arise with reference to form; is form not a basis for delusion, not a cause of ignorance, and so forth... does it lead to Nibbāna?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Should it not be said that “the fetter has the Deathless as its object”?
“Yes. [The opponent asks: “But has it not been said by the Blessed One:

‘One perceives Nibbāna as Nibbāna; having perceived Nibbāna as Nibbāna, one conceives of Nibbāna, one conceives in Nibbāna, one conceives from Nibbāna, one conceives, “Nibbāna is mine,” and one delights in Nibbāna’?”
Is it indeed a sutta? Yes.
Then, consequently, the fetter has the Deathless as its object.
The Discussion on the Deathless Object is finished.
